mounts.title: Mount Folder
mounts.description: Links a folder outside the project into its mounts folder, for large files. The link never goes into git, and the files stay where they are.
mounts.providers: Fully supported for Claude and Codex. Other agents may ask for permission before they use its files.
mounts.nameHint: Shows up in the project as mounts/{{name}}
mounts.unmountConfirm: Only the link mounts/{{name}} is removed. The files in {{target}} stay where they are. A session that is running, or still has background tasks or loops running, can reach the folder until its next message starts a new process.
mounts.adoptableHint: These links are already in mounts/ (made in a terminal, say). Register one to manage it here.
mounts.truncated: Not every file is listed: the mounted folder is too large or too slow to list in full.
mounts.browseIncomplete: Not every folder is listed: this folder is large or slow to read, and {{checked}} of its {{total}} items were checked in time. You can still type the path in "Folder to mount".
mounts.nodeBrokenTitle: Broken mount → {{target}}. {{status}}: right-click to repair or unmount.

validation.nameInvalid: The name can't contain slashes or special characters, or be only dots.

toast.unmountedRowOnly: {{name}} is no longer registered. No link made by this app was at mounts/{{name}}, so nothing there was touched.

errors.invalidName: That name can't be used for a mount.
errors.nameTaken: A mount with that name already exists.
errors.spotTaken: mounts/{{name}} already holds a file, folder or link that isn't a mount. Move it out of the way, or pick another name.
errors.spotTakenByLink: mounts/{{name}} is a link that isn't registered yet. Register it below, or pick another name.
errors.repairSpotTaken: mounts/{{name}} is now a real file or folder, not the link. Move it out of the way and repair again, or unmount.
errors.targetNotFound: That folder doesn't exist or doesn't answer (an offline network share?).
errors.browseUnavailable: This folder can't be opened: it doesn't exist, doesn't answer (an offline network share?), or you aren't allowed to read it.
errors.targetBusy: That folder couldn't be checked in time: its network share is busy (reading a large folder, say), or offline shares are holding up the checks. Try again in a moment.
errors.targetNotDirectory: That path is not a folder.
errors.targetForbidden: System folders, private folders such as ~/.ssh, and folders that contain them can't be mounted. For your home folder, pick a folder inside it.
errors.targetLoop: The folder can't be the project itself, a folder inside it, or a folder that contains it.
errors.mountsDirInUse: The project already has a mounts folder of its own. Rename it, then try again.
errors.mountsDirTracked: The project's mounts folder is tracked by git, so mounts can't be added there.
errors.generic: Something went wrong with the mount.

git.label: Repository
git.newRepoHelp: Runs git init in the folder and commits the template files as the first commit. If the folder is already a Git repository, the files are added but not committed.
git.importGithubHelp: Clones the repository into a subfolder named after it, then adds the template files there without committing them. They show up in Source Control for review.

step3.newWithClone: The repository will be cloned from this folder.
step3.newEmpty: The workspace will be added to your project list and will be available for Claude/Cursor sessions.
step3.gitInitCommit: New repository, first commit with the template files (left uncommitted if the folder is already a repository)
step3.gitCloneUncommitted: Clone, then add the template files uncommitted
step3.keepsExisting: Files that already exist are left as they are.
step3.creatingWithTemplate: Creating the project and adding the template files…

result.title: Project created
result.summary: The project is in your list. A few things need a look.
result.skippedUnsafe: the path goes through a symlink or leads outside the project
result.gitInitialized: Created a Git repository and committed the template files.
result.gitInitializedUncommitted: Created a Git repository. Nothing was committed.
result.gitAlreadyRepository: The folder was already a Git repository, so the new files are left uncommitted.
result.gitAlreadyRepositoryNoFiles: The folder was already a Git repository.
result.gitCloned: The template files are uncommitted in the clone. Review them in Source Control.
result.gitIdentityMissing: Git has no name and email set, so nothing was committed. Set them in Settings → Git, then commit the files.
result.gitNotFound: Git is not installed on the server, so no repository was created.
result.gitInitFailed: git init failed, so no repository was created.
result.gitCommitFailed: The first commit failed. The files are written but not committed.
result.insideParentRepository: The folder is inside another Git repository, so no new repository was created in it.
result.templateApplyFailed: The template files couldn't be written. The project was created without them.
